takeaways.title: 1. Jesus as Supreme Prophet and Foundation of the Church
takeaways.description: Across the opening days of study, Scripture establishes that Jesus Christ is the supreme Prophet who uniquely embodies the Word made flesh. The New Testament church was established on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Himself as the chief cornerstone.
bulletPoints: Jesus fulfills Moses' prophecy (Deut. 18:15) as the definitive divine Prophet, Priest, and King whose authority surpasses all human institutions.
Unlike Old Testament prophets who delivered preparatory messages, Jesus delivers full divine revelation in His person and ministry (Heb. 1:1–3).
The apostolic foundation and prophetic ministry complement each other to build a unified, enduring church body (Eph. 2:20).

egwConnection.note: In Christ is the fullness of the Godhead bodily. All prophetic revelation throughout biblical history finds its center, truth, and vindication in His life, death, and resurrection.

takeaways.title: 2. Functions of New Testament Prophets in Local Congregations
takeaways.description: New Testament prophets operated within local church congregations to provide spiritual guidance, encouragement, warning, and moral exhortation. Prophetic ministry was given to equip believers, protect against deceptive snares, and foster Christlike character.
bulletPoints: New Testament prophets functioned alongside pastors and teachers to edify, exhort, and comfort the flock of God.
The prophetic gift was distributed without gender partiality, as demonstrated by the prophetess Anna and Philip's four prophesying daughters (Acts 21:9).
Prophetic messages were never intended to supersede Scripture, but to guide the church in applying biblical truths faithfully.

egwConnection.note: The gifts of the Spirit are given to the church for its protection, unity, and completion in love until the Lord's return.
egwConnection.source: The Acts of the Apostles, p. 550

takeaways.title: 3. Testing False Prophets and Centering on God's Word
takeaways.description: In the closing days, the lesson warns against deceptive false prophets who arise in the last days. Every prophetic claim must be tested by biblical fruit, loyalty to Jesus' commandments, and strict fidelity to Sola Scriptura.
bulletPoints: Jesus warned that deceptive signs and wonders would emerge in the last days to deceive even the elect if possible (Matt. 24:24).
Disciples must test spirits according to Sola Scriptura: 'To the law and to the testimony; if they speak not according to this word, there is no light in them' (Isa. 8:20).
The end-time remnant church is recognized by keeping the commandments of God and having the testimony of Jesus, which is the Spirit of Prophecy (Rev. 12:17, 19:10).

egwConnection.note: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. God's Word is the detector of all error.
